examples.name: Sample — warn
paragraphs: $ typeset in its own column track, separate from the digits, throughout the balance sheet. It is printed only on the first row of each block and on the grand total, so only those values carry it. The stub header is italic. The row labels are printed flush left, without indentation, so every label is level 0.

examples.name: Sample — an operator in its own track
paragraphs: The Outlook table prints $5.70 Billion | +/- | $300 Million as three ruled cells, and 1.26 Billion spanning all three on the last row. The +/- track is the range dash of this rule in another costume: one value, one cell. Merged, the GAAP and Non-GAAP ranges each become one column and the reconciling amount sits between them; the row labels are bold.

examples.name: Sample — a line-number column in the middle
paragraphs: LINE # runs 1 to 22 in a column between the labels and the first year, not at the left edge. A marker gutter keeps its column wherever the page puts it. The column headers are italic except FOR THE PERIOD ENDED; the empty spacer track between 2023 and 2024 prints nothing and is not a column.

examples.name: Sample — v. in its own track
paragraphs: A court daily list: time, case number and party, v., the other party, hearing type. The v. column carries the same token on every row that has two parties and nothing on the rows that do not — a separator track, like the range dash, so it joins the two parties in one cell. Rows with a single In the matter of… line then take the same shape.
